_comment: One call square, three templates plus a default. The square does not BRANCH — one arrow out, one lead, one visit counter — but WHICH template the lead carries is a question asked of facts already in hand. template_rules is an if/else-if ladder judged in document order: the first arm whose conditions ALL hold names the template, and the square's own template_id is the `else`, so no arm holding fires the default rather than parking the run. Conditions within one arm are ANDed; OR is two arms naming the SAME template — arms 2 and 3 are one rule written as two, because a predicate has no `or`. The fields are the run's rendered variables, named by the LAST segment of the catalog path (payload.products.category -> context.category); the grammar is flat, so context.category, never context.products.category. A rendered list variable is ABSENT when its item_where kept nothing, which is exactly what `not_exists` asks — context.category exists only for a customer whose product the category filter kept, and context.brand is absent for a customer with no product at all. context.event_name is the MOST RECENT letter's, not the founding one's: a run that entered on LINE_INITIATED and later heard LINE_OFFERED is judged on LINE_OFFERED when the call finally fires. A merchant whose own catalog registers INITIATED rather than LINE_INITIATED swaps those topic strings and nothing else — the call square is unchanged.
